speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient presenting with a limp and localized pain, but no fever or acute distress. To begin our evaluation, can you tell me exactly where on your body it hurts and does the pain happen only when you walk?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the pain is in the left knee but you are favoring that leg, would you also feel pain when I press gently on the knee cap or just below it? Additionally, has he experienced any pain in his thigh or hip joint?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calve-Perthes Disease. 

The presentation of a 7-year-old male with an insidious onset of left knee pain, limp, and no fever or trauma is classic for Perthes disease, which typically presents with referred knee pain originating from the hip. While a physical exam was just initiated, the clinical picture strongly points to this etiology over other causes like septic arthritis or acute trauma. No further questions are needed to reach this conclusion based on the age, symptoms, and lack of systemic signs.
